page.title: Audition
page.purpose: Compare the takes from one batch against each other and decide which to keep. This is the scenario's defining surface: composition returns a set, and selection is the quality mechanism.

priorities.statement: Takes are peers. Nothing in the ordering, sizing, or labelling implies one is better — the interface never pre-picks, ranks, or scores on the caller's behalf. Selecting is an act the operator performs.
Takes play without leaving the list, so comparison is direct rather than remembered.
Every take's provenance is reachable: model, licence lane, applied rung, seed, and both the caption as authored and as sent.
Rejecting a take is as cheap as accepting one. 'Give me a different one' is the most likely next action and must regenerate nothing.
A degraded take is labelled, so reduced-rung output is never mistaken for full-quality output.
Every state is legible without relying on audio or colour alone, and playback position is announced to assistive technology.

states.description: The batch is still producing takes; completed ones are already auditionable.
The batch ended early; the completed takes are kept and usable.

claims.statement: Takes are presented in a stable, non-evaluative order with no take visually privileged, and none is pre-selected.
Every take exposes its model, licence lane, applied rung, seed, and both captions.
A take generated at a reduced rung is labelled with that rung.
Discard is available directly on every take, not hidden behind a menu or a confirmation flow.
A batch that ended early states that the completed takes are kept and usable.
A take plays in place; comparing two takes never requires leaving the list.
Playback state and position are available as text and to assistive technology, not by audio alone.
